data.cultural_impact: In Islamic tradition, the name "Aydah" gains cultural significance through its connection to the famous Surah Al-Baqarah (Chapter 2) of the Quran, known as "The Cow". This Surah bears a total of 286 verses and the 85th to 91st verses are collectively referred to as 'Ayat Al-Kursi' (The Ayah or Verse of the Throne), which describes Allah's supremacy and His right to be worshiped. Naming a child "Aydah" could be seen as a reminder of divine comfort and protection, rooted in faith and reverence for Allah's Word.
data.spiritual_significance: From the spiritual perspective, the name "Aydah" holds profound significance as it conveys the idea of submission to Allah's will. It is a reminder of Allah's infinite power and wisdom, and serves as a source of strength and guidance for the individual striving to live a purposeful life in accordance with Islamic teachings. The name "Aydah" symbolizes the faith community's aspiration to rise above worldly distractions and be exalted in Allah's presence, understanding that all revelations (ayat) in the Quran are ultimately from Allah.
